outOfScope.reason: The live API acceptance suite: it waits on a real cloud by design. Each of its waits has a row in docs/development/live-acceptance.md, 'Real-time waits'.
The live API proofs: they wait on a real cloud by design (docs/development/live-acceptance.md, 'Real-time waits').
The live API suite's library; lib/clock.ts is the real clock that the acceptance self-test (acceptance-runner.spec.ts, in scope) replaces with FakeClock.
The live browser proof: it waits on a real cloud and a real sign-in by design. Its *.test.ts files are non-live Jest tests and stay in scope.

The live iOS proof (HAR-169): it waits on a real cloud, a real sign-in and pushed readings by design; each bound is a row of 'The iOS proof's waits' in docs/development/live-acceptance.md. Only this target: MeatGeekUITests and MeatGeekKit's tests stay in scope.
The guard's own fixtures: each violating fixture breaks a rule on purpose, so the guard's tests can see it fail.

exceptions.reason: internal/await is the hang guard itself: Guard(t) reads how long is left before t.Deadline() (go test -timeout) to give up shortly before it, so a stuck wait fails naming its condition. No test's verdict depends on it.
internal/await's guard channel: it closes at Guard(t), just before the test binary's own deadline. It is the hang guard, not a per-wait deadline.
Same line as above: the real timer that fires the hang guard. Only a wait that would otherwise hang past go test -timeout ever sees it.

HAR-125's test runs the OLD `writer | grep -q` form on purpose, on a 2 MiB input that makes it fail every time, to prove the failure is real; it asserts on PIPESTATUS, under `|| true`. The new here-string form is tested right after it.

A condition poll with no deadline of its own (the rule's third way to wait): the 'parallel' fixture re-checks every 10 ms until all copies have written their marker, bounded only by the test-repeat-harness suite's hang guard. fs.watch was tried first and drops the last event on macOS.
